Rewrote to the batch-canonical 'Salt' (bid salt, brand Morton), buy string '2 1/4 tsp fine sea salt, divided', which keeps the prose truthful. Salt is zero-macro so no stat number moved. The two source salt lines (chimichurri 3 g fine sea salt + sheet pan 11 g) are combined into one 14 g shopping line, divided in the steps.

OLIVE OIL COMBINED: the source's two oil lines (chimichurri 125 g + sheet pan 64 g) are one bottle to a shopper, so they are booked as a single 189 g line (7/8 cup, divided). Grams and macros are the exact sum; the steps divide it (about 9 tbsp into the chimichurri, about 5 tbsp reserved for the vegetables). EVOO and pure olive oil share the olive-oil commodity per the mapper.

EVERY BOUGHT INGREDIENT IS USED BY A STEP and no step uses anything unbought. Walked both directions: steak (make_it 4, 7), sweet potatoes (5, 6), broccolini (6), olive oil (3 chimichurri + 5 potatoes + 6 broccolini, divided), red wine vinegar (3), fresh cilantro (3), fresh parsley (3), garlic (3), fresh oregano (3), red pepper flakes (3), salt (3 chimichurri + 5,6 vegetables, divided). The '1/2 cup chimichurri divided' source line is the sub-recipe yield of the herb section, not a purchased ingredient (mapper confirmed the scaled component mass matches the call); it is NOT a shopping line, it is made in step 3 and divided across steps 4 and 8. No separate chimichurri is bought.

SHOP_SMART makes NO per-ounce, leftover, or lasts-several-batches claim, so no bullet requires a cost_lines entry to prove it; every statement is grounded in the recipe's own buy amount, package sizes referenced generically and never with a per-line cost. Clear of the 2026-08-15 audit failures. Re-walk the bullets against cost_lines once costed before publish.

BROCCOLI SWAP is a source-sanctioned WRITER OPTION, mentioned in shop_smart only. Broccolini maps to its own broccolini commodity (carried per Rule B, Baker's only, 1 of 7 stores); the source's comment section sanctions plain broccoli as an equal swap. Prose names broccolini as the ingredient and offers plain broccoli as the stand-in if a store does not carry broccolini. No step calls for broccoli; the bought and cooked vegetable is broccolini.

Two real cost lines are unwired: 'Broccolini' and 'Fresh Parsley' have NO row in db\ingredients.json and NO entry in ingredient-map.json, even though both commodities (broccolini $3.99/each, fresh-parsley $0.99/each) DO exist on the live feed. cost-recipes reads item knowledge from db\ingredients.json, so it cannot connect the item to the bid and will DROP both from the costed row at $0.00. The rendered cost_ps in this build is therefore a FLOOR, understated by broccolini and parsley until the mapper/registrar wires the two item->bid rows and the recipe is recosted. PORTION METHOD adapted to a sheet pan: weigh the empty pan first, weigh it loaded at the end, subtract, divide by 14. The chimichurri drizzle is added before the final weigh so it is counted in the portion.

prose.intro_html: Chimichurri is what happens when a steak decides to dress up. It is nothing fancier than fresh herbs, garlic, red wine vinegar, and good olive oil buzzed into a bright green sauce, and it pulls a double shift here. Half of it marinates the steak before it hits the pan, and the other half gets spooned over the top at the end. Everything roasts on one sheet pan next to sweet potatoes and broccolini, so there is one pan to wash and nothing to stand over. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 35 grams of carbs. That is a steakhouse plate that fits inside a meal-prep container.
shop_smart: Three and a half pounds of steak is the anchor. Sirloin or flank both work, so buy whichever the case has cheaper that week, and reach for the big family pack instead of the small trays so you are paying for beef and not for packaging. This is where most of the money and all of the protein live.

About nine sweet potatoes carry the plate. Size matters here more than usual. Reach for potatoes around a half pound each, not the little ones, because that heft is what fills out the serving and keeps this from eating like a light lunch. Roasted whole and then split, they turn sweet and creamy with no peeling.

A couple bunches of broccolini round out the pan. Broccolini roasts fast and crisps at the tips, which is exactly what you want next to a rich steak. If your store does not carry it, plain broccoli cut into spears works the same way and roasts on the same pan.

Fresh herbs are the whole point of the sauce. You want a bunch each of cilantro and parsley and a little fresh oregano, all blended down into the chimichurri. Buy them fresh, not dried, because dried herbs turn this sauce muddy and flat. You use only a small handful of each, all blended down into the green sauce.

Olive oil, red wine vinegar, garlic, red pepper flakes, and sea salt finish it. These are pantry and produce backbone you most likely already keep on hand, so they barely move the cart. The vinegar and the garlic are what give chimichurri its bite, and a pinch of red pepper flakes brings just enough heat to notice.
make_it: Weigh your empty sheet pan and write the number down. You will weigh it loaded at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which is the only honest way to portion a whole pan of food.
Heat the oven to 350 degrees F.

Make the chimichurri first. Put the red wine vinegar, cilantro, parsley, garlic, fresh oregano, red pepper flakes, a half teaspoon of the fine sea salt, and about nine tablespoons of the olive oil in a blender, holding back the rest of the oil for the vegetables. Blend until it is smooth and bright green, then set it aside. You will divide it in two directions.
Slice the steak into half-inch strips, drop them in a large bowl, and toss with about a third of the chimichurri to marinate while the potatoes get going.
Rub the whole sweet potatoes with a couple tablespoons of the reserved olive oil and a little of the sea salt, lay them on the sheet pan, and bake for 45 minutes.

Pull the pan out and cut each sweet potato in half, spreading the halves across the pan. Toss the broccolini with the last of the reserved olive oil and sprinkle the potatoes and broccolini with the rest of the sea salt.

Lift the steak out of its marinade and lay the strips on the pan among the vegetables. Slide it back in and bake for 30 minutes, until the steak is cooked the way you like it and the broccolini tips are crisp.
Drizzle the remaining chimichurri over the steak and vegetables, then weigh the loaded pan and portion as below.
prose.portion_html: Set the loaded sheet pan on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total, steak and vegetables and sauce together. Divide that number by 14 and give each container that exact weight, aiming for an even share of steak, sweet potato, and broccolini. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a chimichurri steak dinner that most people only order out. The steak and the sweet potatoes carry the plate, and the green sauce is what makes it taste like more than the sum of its parts.

head.description: Chimichurri steak sheet pan dinner for meal prep: sirloin or flank steak marinated in a fresh herb chimichurri and roasted with sweet potatoes and broccolini, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 35 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: chimichurri steak, sheet pan steak dinner, chimichurri sheet pan, low carb meal prep, high protein beef dinner
steps: Weigh the empty sheet pan and note the number for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350 degrees F.

Blend the red wine vinegar, cilantro, parsley, garlic, fresh oregano, red pepper flakes, some of the fine sea salt, and most of the olive oil into a smooth chimichurri, holding back oil for the vegetables.
Slice the steak into half-inch strips and toss with about a third of the chimichurri to marinate.
Rub the sweet potatoes with reserved olive oil and sea salt and bake for 45 minutes.
Cut the potatoes, toss the broccolini with the last of the oil and salt, and add both to the pan.
Lay the marinated steak on the pan and bake for 30 minutes.
Drizzle the remaining chimichurri over everything, then weigh the pan and divide across 14 containers.
